Chest drain insertion. Assisting the doctor, step by step.
Step one. Know why a chest drain is needed: pneumothorax, haemothorax, pleural effusion, or after thoracic surgery.

Step two. Know the procedure: the pleural anatomy, site selection, positioning and equipment set-up. Know water-seal and suction-assisted systems, the complications, bleeding, infection, surgical emphysema and lung injury, and the emergencies, such as tension pneumothorax or equipment failure.

Step three. Prepare the patient. Identify the patient correctly, and make sure the doctor has obtained informed consent. Give analgesia as prescribed. Assemble all items and check expiry dates. Perform hand hygiene, put on non-sterile gloves, position the patient, and place an Inco-pad under the chest.
Step four. Critical point. Perform hand hygiene and put on protective equipment. Prepare the water seal drainage system, filling the water seal to the marked level, and make the connections.
Step five. Critical point. Prepare the chest drain set on a sterile field using aseptic technique, and assist the doctor throughout the procedure.
Step six. Connect the prepared drainage system to the chest tube, and connect it to wall suction as ordered. Keep the unit upright, and below the level of the chest.
Step seven. Critical point. Arrange a chest X-ray urgently. Discard sharps into the correct container, clean the trolley, and perform hand hygiene.

Step eight. Critical point. After the procedure, monitor vital signs as per policy, and give adequate analgesia. Check the drainage system regularly: the amount and colour of drainage, any air leak, and the water levels in the suction and air leak chambers.
If the patient suddenly deteriorates, for example with a tension pneumothorax or equipment failure, call for help and follow the emergency protocol.
Step ten. Stay calm and supportive, protect the patient's dignity, respond to any discomfort, and ask for guidance when you are unsure.

Step eleven. Document the date, time, indication and site, the doctor and the assisting staff, the baseline assessment and consent check, the tube type and size, the drainage set-up, any complications, and your observations after the procedure.
Watch, take the quiz, then get signed off.
